title: Minimax Endpoint Estimation for Panel Count Data with a Random Terminal Audit
banked_reason: Cold D0.5 tier subfield below field floor (paper score ceiling 6.8 < 7.4; salvageable=false); decision panel REVISE findings remain unrepaired, although math referee PASS.
gap_reasons: The promised all-κ minimax order is not delivered: for κ=0 with positive vanishing audits the theorem leaves only a lower/upper bracket and explicitly leaves logarithmic attainability open, so the current kernel is narrower than the headline frontier.

The theorem needs a substantive closest-work comparison with the listed informative-visit/censoring panel-count literature (especially WangMaYan2013AEE) and an explicit theorem-level distinction; a bibliography entry without a relevance sentence is insufficient positioning.
proof_attempt_summary: The discovery phase derived the inverse-visit estimator, finite-sample coverage, and a full observed-likelihood Poisson lower construction, then sharpened the moving-audit analysis. The κ=0 positive-vanishing audit case remained an honest lower/upper bracket rather than the promised matched frontier, and the decision referee's positioning finding was not repaired; the math referee passed, but the panel as a whole did not establish soundness. A new multiscale upper estimator and proof would be needed to close the principal gap.
tldr: A known random fraction \(\pi_n\) of subjects receives a terminal count audit in addition to the sparse ordinary visit. The explicit precision blend has finite-sample bias-aware coverage and constructive upper order \(\min\{n^{-(s+1)/(2s+\kappa+3)},(n\pi_n)^{-1/2}\}\). A legal fixed-sample pair using the complete audited Poisson likelihood matches this order for \(\kappa>0\), for the \(\kappa=0\) no-audit case, and throughout the flat negligible-audit edge \(\pi_n\log n=O(n^{-1/(2s+3)})\), with constants depending on the bounded ratio; fixed-positive audit fractions give root-\(n\) inference. For other positive vanishing audit fractions at \(\kappa=0\), the rational-profile pair yields the lower information \(n b^{2(s+1)}[b+\pi_n\{1+\log(1+\delta/(b\vee\pi_n))\}]\), producing an explicit bracket whose logarithmic attainability remains open.
gap: Classical degenerate-design regression supplies the no-audit exponent, while regular two-phase causal theory assumes a second-phase probability bounded away from zero. Neither literature determines how a vanishing terminal-audit fraction interacts with sparse endpoint visits in the full panel-count likelihood.
fill: Construct a combined, history-valid estimator and finite-sample interval; prove a two-channel marked-Poisson lower bound; and characterize the minimax and honest-length phase transition as a function of \(n\), \(\pi_n\), \(s\), and \(\kappa\).
